teams.heading: Fiji sit bottom of the log following their third consecutive loss
teams.body: Fiji remain at the bottom of the log in 12th place. In their opening three matches of this tournament, the side has suffered three consecutive defeats. They have conceded 145 points across those three fixtures. In contrast, they have scored 49 points of their own during this period, leaving them with a point differential of minus 96. This difficult run follows a 17-33 loss to Scotland in their last match. Historically, the highest-ever position the team has reached in the world rankings is No. 7, achieved in 2023.

teams.body: Munster confirmed last week that Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley will remain sidelined until the new year due to a vascular injury. The 26-year-old has been out of action since April, missing July's internationals. Crowley's prolonged absence rules him out of November's tests against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan prioritised his long-term recovery, stating, "ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority."

teams.heading: Gerónimo Prisciantelli and Joaquín Moro tries fail to prevent Australia loss
teams.body: Los Pumas suffered a 21-27 defeat to Australia in San Salvador de Jujuy on Saturday, highlighting a troubling trend for the national side. Despite tries from Gerónimo Prisciantelli, Joaquín Moro and Boris Wenger—all converted by Santiago Carreras—Argentina failed to capitalise on a second-half yellow card for the Wallabies. The result means the team have won only once in their last five matches, all of which were played on home soil. A rematch in Mendoza offers an immediate opportunity to address the slump.

teams.heading: JRLO officials roll back eligibility restrictions for Timothy Lafaele and teammates
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has abandoned contentious plans to reclassify naturalised citizens as foreign players following a legal challenge and widespread backlash. A settlement reached in the Tokyo District Court ensures that foreign-born players who acquired Japanese nationality by May 2025 remain in the top domestic eligibility category. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji admitted, "We lacked communication with players who would be adversely affected by the changes." The U-turn protects the status of Brave Blossoms veterans including Timothy Lafaele and Jiwon Gu.

lead.why: The JRLO's reversal on player eligibility rules follows a major legal challenge by national team stars and impacts the domestic league's structure.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie’s scrum tactics allegations drawing sharp protocol rebuke from Rassie Erasmus
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has hit back at Dave Rennie, accusing the New Zealand head coach of attempting to influence referees through the media rather than using official channels. Following Saturday’s 33-26 loss in the second Test in Cape Town, Rennie alleged the Springboks were “walking around” at the scrum. Erasmus, who initially responded with a series of expletives, today insisted that Rennie must follow World Rugby protocols, adding that “one can’t make opinion facts” in the media before Saturday’s third Test in Soweto.

lead.why: The escalation of the Rennie-Erasmus feud over scrum legality and media protocols is the dominant talking point following the second Test.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus restores Ox Nché and Malcolm Marx following Dave Rennie spat
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has named a reinforced front row for Saturday’s third Test against New Zealand, restoring Ox Nché, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw to the starting XV. The selection follows a heated exchange with All Blacks coach Dave Rennie, who accused the Springboks of illegal scrum tactics during South Africa’s 33-26 victory in Cape Town. Erasmus dismissed the allegations, stating, "one can't make opinion facts" while urging New Zealand to use official World Rugby protocols for grievances rather than the media.
